title: Queue Storage from C#
description: Use Azure Queue Storage to offload work from an ASP.NET Core request into a background consumer.

data.text: Queue Storage provides simple FIFO messaging. In ASP.NET Core, queues are useful for offloading slow work like email, image processing, or report generation out of the HTTP request path.

items: Messages are up to 64 KB in size
Queues are scoped to a storage account
Visibility timeout prevents other consumers from reading the same message

data.title: Add a message and process it

data.text: A common pattern is an ASP.NET Core API that enqueues work and a background worker that processes it. You can host the worker in the same app using `IHostedService`.

data.title: Background queue worker
data.content: This worker runs inside the same ASP.NET Core host.

data.title: Queue an email job
data.description: When a user registers, enqueue a welcome email job instead of sending it synchronously.
steps: Save the user to a database or in-memory list
Serialize an email job to JSON and send it to the queue
Log the enqueued message and return 202 Accepted
data.expectedOutcome: The API returns immediately while the email job waits in the queue.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Queue Storage decouples slow work from HTTP requests
Messages are simple strings; pass JSON for structured data
Always delete messages after successful processing
Use `IHostedService` for queue workers inside ASP.NET Core
data.takeaway: Queues make your API faster and more reliable by moving non-critical work outside the request pipeline.
